sources.entry: Viseron - Self-hosted, local-only NVR and AI Computer Vision software. With features such as object detection, motion detection, face recognition and more, it gives you the power to keep an eye on your home, office or any other place you want to monitor. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Viseron is a self-hosted, local-only NVR (network video recorder) with AI computer vision features such as object detection, motion detection and face recognition.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Viseron as self-hosted, local-only network video recorder and computer vision software. It states that features include object detection, motion detection and face recognition, aimed at monitoring a home, office or other location. Getting started is described as spinning up a Docker container and editing the configuration file through a built-in web interface. Functionality is split into components, which the README says can be browsed in a Component Explorer. The README points to external documentation for setup instructions and to a Discord server for help.
how_to_run: Spin up a Docker container for Viseron
Edit the configuration file using the built-in web interface
See the documentation for full getting-started instructions
notable: Local-only operation; the README describes it as self-hosted and local only
Functionality is modular via components, browsable in a Component Explorer
Configuration is edited through a built-in web interface
Covers object detection, motion detection and face recognition
caveats: README gives no detailed hardware or camera requirements
Full setup details are in external documentation, not the README
Docker is the only deployment method the README names
keywords: keep an eye on my home
